Report_ID: Mazur functional ankle score at 6 weeks
Title: Functional outcome of surgery for fractures of the ankle: A prospective, randomised comparison of management in a cast or a functional brace
Author: K. A. Egol, R. Dolan, K. J. Koval
Comment: M_diff was computed as 56.5 − 52.4 = 4.1 (brace minus cast) for this simple two-group comparison. SE_diff was computed from the explicitly reported group SDs and sample sizes as sqrt(5.3^2/28 + 7.6^2/27) = 1.773. Hedges g was computed from the explicitly reported means, SDs, and sample sizes (positive favors brace). The paper used a Mann-Whitney U test but did not report the U statistic. Although the instrument is described as a 100-point scale, no explicit minimum is stated, so outcome_scale_min and outcome_scale_max are left null.
Participant type: Skeletally mature patients with a closed, isolated unstable ankle fracture requiring surgical stabilisation
Recruitment source: 60 consecutive patients undergoing open reduction and internal fixation at the Hospital for Joint Diseases
Outcome measurement: Ankle grading system of Mazur, Schwartz and Simon; described as a scale of 100 points, with 50 for pain, 40 for function, and 10 for range of movement
Outcome variable: Mazur functional ankle score at 6 weeks
outcome_family: activity limitation at end of treatment
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better function; observed effect favors removable ankle support.

Title: Ankle Performance after Ankle Fracture: A Randomized Study of Early Mobilization
Author: Hans Tropp and Rolf Norlin
Comment: M_diff was calculated as brace mean minus plaster mean (77 − 70 = 7) from the two explicitly reported group means. Per-group analysed sample sizes were not explicitly stated alongside this outcome, so they were left null; consequently no standardized effect size or SE_diff was calculated. The paper states only that the between-group difference was not significant and gives no exact P value. The maximal score is stated as 100 points, but a complete fixed 0–100 range is not explicitly stated, so scale bounds were left null.; n_treatment(15) and n_control(15) assumed equal split from n_total=30
domain: Orthopedics; surgically managed ankle fracture rehabilitation
Participant type: Adults aged 18–60 years with Danis-Weber group B or C ankle fractures treated by open reduction and internal fixation
Outcome measurement: Modified Olerud score for subjective and objective ankle symptoms
outcome_family: activity limitation at end of treatment
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better function; observed effect favors removable ankle support.

Report_ID: Olerud Molander ankle score (OMAS) at 16 weeks
Title: Use of cast immobilisation versus removable brace in adults with an ankle fracture: multicentre randomised controlled trial
Author: Kearney et al.
Comment: The supplied paper text reports overall mixed operative/non-operative 16-week OMAS means and SDs, but the synthesis contract requires surgically managed patients only. Numerical operative-subgroup results are only referenced to supplementary file 3, Table 6 and are not present in the supplied text. Randomised operative counts (182 per arm) are not used because final analysed subgroup Ns are not stated. Therefore no surgery-only effect estimate or SMD inputs can be extracted without the supplement.; regression: no convertible statistic — need t-value for coefficient, b+SE(b), standardised β, r, η², or means+SDs
Design Type: Pragmatic multicentre parallel-group randomised controlled trial
Study Environment: 20 trauma units in the UK National Health Service
Medium: Removable fixed-angle ankle brace versus below-knee plaster cast
Content length: Minimum of three weeks assigned support; primary outcome at 16 weeks
Participant type: Adults with an acute ankle fracture treated operatively
Recruitment source: Trauma services at 20 UK NHS trusts
Outcome measurement: Self-administered nine-item Olerud Molander ankle score; higher scores indicate better function

Title: Early Weightbearing and Range of Motion vs Non-Weightbearing and Immobilization After Open Reduction and Internal Fixation of Unstable Ankle Fractures: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Niloofar Dehghan et al.
Comment: M_diff was validly computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean = 32 − 45 = −13 for this simple two-group comparison. Report_ID: Olerud and Molander ankle score at six weeks
Title: Use of a Cast Compared with a Functional Ankle Brace After Operative Treatment of an Ankle Fracture
Author: Lehtonen et al.
Comment: M_diff was computed as brace mean minus cast mean (52 − 54 = −2) from explicit means in this simple two-group parallel comparison. The paper reports only that the difference was not significant; no exact p-value or test statistic is provided. Although the instrument is described as a “100-point scale,” explicit minimum and maximum values are not stated, so scale bounds were left null.
Participant type: Patients with an acute displaced or unstable Weber type-A or B ankle fracture treated operatively
Recruitment source: One hundred consecutive patients treated operatively at the authors’ hospital
Outcome measurement: Olerud and Molander ankle scoring system; higher scores indicate better ankle function
Outcome variable: Olerud and Molander ankle score at six weeks
outcome_family: activity limitation at end of treatment
effect_direction: Higher scores indicate better function; observed effect favors non-removable cast.
